title: The Electrification Target
paragraphs: One of the main items under discussion at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya is a voluntary global target of raising electricity's share of final energy consumption to 35 per cent by 2035. The target is based on analysis by the International Energy Agency and the International Renewable Energy Agency of what is needed to keep the 1.5C warming limit within reach, and it has attracted at least 14 explicit endorsements, among them Australia, Germany and Norway, whereas the UK and the EU have acknowledged the need for electrification without formally backing the pledge. Some developing countries, such as Fiji, welcomed the idea but stressed that support would be required to deliver it.

Meeting it will be demanding. Electricity currently accounts for an estimated 23.4 per cent of the energy delivered to consumers, a share that has risen by only 6.7 percentage points since 2000, so the rate of electrification would have to quadruple compared with the first quarter of the century and triple compared with the years from 2020 to 2025. Judit Hecke of the German think tank New Climate Institute considers such an acceleration possible, but says the challenge lies in getting policies, investment and infrastructure to move at the same pace. Renewable energy offers encouragement: in 2024, nearly 32 per cent of global electricity came from renewable sources, against 18 per cent in 2000, and capacity has grown from 0.8 to 5.2 terawatts. Hecke points out, however, that the target counts electricity however it is generated, so a country could make progress while still relying heavily on coal and gas, and she argues that electrification, renewables and energy efficiency must be pursued together.

options.text: Electrification has been moving faster than renewable power generation.
The 35 per cent target will be reached by continuing the existing trend.
options.explanation: Mevcut hızın dört katına çıkması gerektiği söylenir.

options.text: Past progress is too slow to reach the target without a large acceleration.
options.explanation: Pay 2000'den beri yalnızca 6,7 puan arttığı için hedefe ulaşmak hızın katlanmasını gerektirir.

options.text: Most of the increase in electricity's share came from renewable sources.
options.explanation: Payın artışının kaynağı bu şekilde belirtilmez.

sources.claim: COP31'de gönüllü 35'e 35 elektrifikasyon hedefi; en az 14 açık destek; elektriğin payı yüzde 23,4, 2000'den beri 6,7 puan artış; hız dört katına çıkmalı; yenilenebilir payı 2024'te yaklaşık yüzde 32; Hecke'nin görüşleri.
sources.source: New Scientist, 21 Kasım 2026, s.6 (Shosha Adie, 'Can we meet COP's electrification goal?')
